doc: WO-157 (Onsen step 4b): the ONE receiver-side wake decision as data. decideWake (wake-decide.ts) reads the item's own fields (kind, urgency, no_reply, deadline, sender, refs) and this agent's one state (member: Onsen's status of the main; main_offered; lane_free; owner, gate, worker_topics: what the router's own tables say about this item) and returns where it goes: main_now | main_after_step | lane:<kind> | ledger (record only) | held:<wall|offline|starting|waiting|stuck> (then where it goes when released). Rules are read in order, first match wins; an agent's own rules (<workspace>/.lanes/router.json `wake_rules`, and its older router.json rules translated by legacyAgentRules) come first. `to` main/owner/lane:* is resolved by the state map the rule names (`map`). No text prefix decides anything: the kind is the sender's field. `replaces` names the decision points of claude-chiron/knowledge/tg-dialogue/step4-facts.md (#n) and the router rules (R:<id>, lanes-router.fleet.json) whose job the rule takes.

urgency_default.doc: the urgency when the sender filled none (design page: a call interrupts; mail, a scheduled run, an unmarked program notice are ordered; a post on the wall is record only; a state crossing is `state`)

maps.doc: how a destination becomes a target in each member state (design page table, rows 閒置／處理中／等人按、卡住／撞上限／失連). `+offered`: the main is idle but an item is already offered to it (one offer opens one turn). A lane destination goes on in every state but the wall and offline, where it is held and goes to the lane when released.

joey.doc: Joey's own message: as the main, and in the three held states he is told where it is (tell joey)

state.doc: a state crossing of the main itself (keep-warm, stall, restart, resume): it exists to move the main, so a busy, waiting or stuck main still gets it at its next step; the wall and offline hold it

lane.doc: a lane destination: the lanes share the main's account (the wall holds them too); offline holds per the design page (失連：留著)

rules.doc: an admission gate already said no (a peer on hold or over the flood limit, a repeat alert, a mailbox run already waiting, a stopped thread, a second decision): record only. The gates themselves are unchanged; this rule records their verdict as the decision.
lanes switched off (/lanes off): every item reaches the main, as before lanes.

replaces: the main's lane tools (fork, open_worker, fan_out, curate_memory, synthesis)
rules.doc: the main or a lane started it and named its lane: that lane. Not a decision about anyone else's item.
Joey quotes a lane's message or writes in a worker's topic: that lane.
Joey's message: the main (now when idle, after this step when busy; held and told where it is when waiting, stuck or offline).

replaces: #12/#13 the watchdog's own 回合在跑→不戳, checked again on arrival
rules.doc: keep-warm that arrives while the main is in a turn: its cache is being written by that turn; nothing to keep warm. Record only.
a state of the main crossed a line: the main, by the state map (a busy, waiting or stuck main gets it after this step; wall and offline hold it).
a mail (and, until 4d retires them, the ring and the reminder that point at the mailbox): the mail lane reads it.

replaces: #10 mail_decision → the lane that asked (L mailDecision)
rules.doc: the main's decision on a card: the lane that asked, on its thread.

replaces: L mailDecision: no lane for the thread
rules.doc: a decision whose asking lane cannot be found: the main does it.
a card entering its due window: information for the main's next digest (the card's own due wake is a `card` item).
a card that can wait (rides every digest until the batch or its due wake) and a run that owed nothing: record only.
a lane hands the main what it cannot do (or the system does at a run's end, a card's due time, the 45-minute batch): the main, by the state map.

replaces: R:mesh-no-reply (now only when the sender says record only; no_reply no longer decides)
rules.doc: the sender said nobody needs to act: record only (rides the main's next digest).
the item belongs to a conversation one of this agent's lines owns (its thread, a reply to our message, the incident a lane handles, the ticket's worker): that line.
an urgent work order: a worker lane for the ticket.
an urgent work order when no worker can be opened (topics off): the main does the work.
a scheduled run (and its nudge): a reflex lane.
a page-tier alert: a reflex lane (repeats and incidents are the gate and owner rules above).
a colleague's call: a reflex lane first; the lane hands the main what it cannot do.

replaces: R:default for programs outside the roster
R:mesh-no-reply for their no_reply notices (the Iris case)
rules.doc: a program outside the roster (Slack waker, reply-watch, crons): a reflex lane handles it (design page decision 2, the recommended default). An agent that wants its program at the main adds its own rule.
anything else: the main.
